quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes it hard to see clearly, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your recovery from headlight glare, and often makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Which behaviors are signs of road rage?

options.text: Deliberately blocking other vehicles.
Flashing headlights.
Cutting off or swerving in front of other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Road rage behaviors include deliberately blocking other drivers, tailgating, flashing headlights, cutting off or swerving in front of other drivers, following another vehicle, and making threats or rude gestures. If you see these actions, give the driver space and do not retaliate.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene immediately.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them without training can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press down directly on the wound to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: In a city, you should look at least ____ block(s) ahead of your vehicle.

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you spot problems before you reach them. In the city, look at least two blocks ahead of your vehicle.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as the traffic direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they face the oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What can you do from the center turn lane?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: This lane is only for left-turning vehicles from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or for driving straight through.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn you about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey first?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over signs, signals, and road markings. Police officers, fire police, road work flag persons, and school crossing guards have the authority to direct traffic.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is approaching or when you are following another vehicle. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need to use more force to steer. Slow down and carefully drive to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way lanes divided by a median. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet away from the tracks. Watch for other warning signs like lowered crossing gates or sounds of an approaching train.

questions.question: Where is the best place to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not let other vehicles crowd your left and right sides.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do first?

options.text: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is empty. Give a turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What is a good rule to remember about passing?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
Try to get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, there is a greater chance of a crash. If you drive faster than traffic around you, you will need to keep passing. Stay with traffic flow, obey speed limits, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs along with alcohol?

options.text: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.
Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
Has no effect on your general driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can harm your brain function and your ability to drive safely. Combining alcohol with drugs makes crashes much more likely.

questions.question: What is true about emergency vehicles?

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles with sirens or horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so wait until you are sure the way is clear before moving.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.
Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Lift your foot off the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have full control. Once the car is steady, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue to drive at the same speed.
Accelerate to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. If you cannot safely change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down near emergency scenes.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats that fit their size. No one is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always keep children properly secured in a seat.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you remain in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be unsafe.

questions.question: How can you prevent highway hypnosis?

options.text: Start your drive well-rested.
Stop regularly, even if you don't feel tired.
Keep your eyes moving.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when drivers get bored on long trips. To prevent it, start your trip rested. Stop regularly, even if you don't think you're tired. Keep your eyes scanning the road to avoid eye strain from looking in one spot too long.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, let that vehicle go first. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. This applies to all passengers and all areas of the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when roads are slippery?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or ice appear. These create slippery roads. When conditions are bad, you may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near children at play, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use extra caution when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
It only works if a green circle light is also on.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, just like a green light. However, you must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see objects 500 feet away.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: If you are thrown from your car during an accident, your chances of being killed are ____ times greater.
questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the best way to prevent injury or death in a crash. If you are thrown from your car, your chances of being killed are 25 times greater.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when drivers act unexpectedly. Talk with other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When should drivers use hand-over-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving activity.
When avoiding a hazard at a high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing, activating signals, turning on the radio, or activating windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel at low speeds.
questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering when turning at low speeds, such as at intersections or when parking. Place your left hand on the wheel between 8 and 9 o'clock and your right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop sign at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate that they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to the driver on your right at a four-way stop if you both arrive at the same time. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the road shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic when you return to the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to dangers ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before you start drinking that you are not going to drive.
Simply say, "No thanks, I'm driving," if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: Decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so you cannot make safe choices after drinking.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful behind large vehicles. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Decrease your speed.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, you must pull off and let faster vehicles pass if traffic is backing up behind you.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the road center mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers can pass if it is safe. Do not pass if oncoming traffic is in your way.
